title: Boss: lost on a new server
summary: Follow relative paths, find big old logs and tell bytes from inodes on a real server.

steps.title: Your first day on prod-7
body: You've been handed SSH access to prod-7, a server you've never seen. Three tickets, each on a real machine: follow a
trail of relative paths someone left behind, list the big old logs before anyone deletes them, and find out whether the
disk is full of bytes or full of files.

steps.title: Follow the breadcrumbs
prompt: The previous admin of prod-7 left a trail of clues in `~/prod7`, starting at `~/prod7/START.txt`. Each clue says where
to go next, **relative to the folder the clue is in**. Some clues are in hidden files.
Follow the trail with `cd`, `ls -a` and `cat`, and write the final code (just the code, like `ABC-123`) into
`~/answers/code.txt`. Careful: other `.clue` files on the server hold decoy codes.

checks.name: code.txt holds the code at the end of the trail
checks.fail: That is not the code at the end of the trail. Start again at `~/prod7/START.txt` and resolve each relative path from the folder of the clue you are reading.

hints: `cd ~/prod7/var/log/nginx && ls -a`: the clue is a dot file. `cat .clue`.
"Up two levels" is `cd ../..`. Extra `.` and doubled `/` in a path change nothing: `../../../../opt/tools/./bin//` is just `~/prod7/opt/tools/bin`.
steps.explain: `..` is resolved against the folder you are in, not against the file you read: that is the whole trick of relative paths. `pwd` after each `cd` is the habit that stops you running `rm` in the wrong place.

steps.title: find: big, old logs
prompt: The disk on prod-7 is filling up. Before deleting anything, the team wants a list of candidates.
Write into `~/answers/big-old.txt` every file under `~/srv` whose name ends in `.log` (lowercase, exactly), that is
**bigger than 1 MiB** and was **not modified in the last 7 days**, one absolute path per line, as `find ~/srv ...` prints them.
Then write into `~/answers/big-old-total.txt` their total size as `du -ch` reports it on its last line (like `12M total`).

checks.name: big-old.txt lists exactly the matching logs
checks.fail: The list does not match. Combine three tests: `-name '*.log'`, `-size +1M` and `-mtime +7`. `api.log.1` does not end in `.log`, and `nightly.LOG` is upper case.

checks.name: big-old-total.txt holds the total
checks.fail: `~/answers/big-old-total.txt` should hold the total of those files, as the last line of `du -ch` prints it.

hints: Tests in a `find` command are ANDed: `find ~/srv -type f -name '*.log' -size +1M -mtime +7`.
`-size +1M` means more than 1 MiB, `-mtime +7` means more than 7 whole days ago. `-iname` would also match `nightly.LOG`, which the task excludes.
For the total: `find ... -print0 | xargs -0 du -ch | tail -n1 > ~/answers/big-old-total.txt`.
steps.explain: `find` with `-size` and `-mtime` turns "what can I delete?" into a list you can review before acting. Always look at the list first, then rerun the same command with `-delete` (or `-exec gzip {} +`).

steps.title: Where did the disk go? Bytes and inodes
prompt: `~/var` stands in for `/var` on prod-7. Two different alerts fired: one for space, one for **inodes** (the number of
files a filesystem can hold: `df -i` shows them; when they run out, writes fail with *No space left on device*
1. `~/answers/biggest.txt`: the name of the folder directly under `~/var` that uses the most **space**.
2. `~/answers/most-files.txt`: the name of the folder directly under `~/var` that holds the most **files** (inodes).
3. Fix the inode problem: delete the session files in `~/var/cache/sessions` that are older than 7 days. Keep the recent ones.

checks.name: biggest.txt names the folder with the most bytes
checks.fail: `~/answers/biggest.txt` should name the biggest folder. `du -xh --max-depth=1 ~/var | sort -h` puts it last.

checks.name: most-files.txt names the folder with the most inodes
checks.fail: `~/answers/most-files.txt` should name the folder with the most files. `du --inodes -x --max-depth=1 ~/var | sort -n` counts files instead of bytes.

checks.name: stale sessions are deleted
checks.fail: There are still session files older than 7 days in `~/var/cache/sessions`.

checks.name: recent sessions are kept
checks.fail: Recent session files were deleted too. Only the ones older than 7 days should go.

hints: `du -xh --max-depth=1 ~/var | sort -h`: `-x` stays on one filesystem, `-h` with `sort -h` sorts human sizes correctly.
`du --inodes --max-depth=1 ~/var | sort -n` counts files. 4000 tiny files take almost no space but 4000 inodes.
`find ~/var/cache/sessions -type f -mtime +7 -delete`. With 2000 files, `rm sess_old_*` might also hit *Argument list too long*; `find -delete` never does.
explain: "Disk full" has two meanings. Bytes: find the fat folder with `du -xh --max-depth=1 | sort -h` and drill down. Inodes:
`df -i` at 100% while `df -h` shows space means millions of tiny files (sessions, cache, mail queue); `du --inodes`
finds them. A third cause is a deleted file a process still holds open, which `lsof +L1` shows (module 4).
